title: Learned structural screening enables a comparative sodium-cathode redox map
summary: Machine-learned interatomic energies screened stacking candidates before first-principles calculations across fifteen sodium layered-oxide chemistries. The resulting comparative map found a largely partner-independent order of redox couples, explaining modeled charge transfer and oxidation sequences. These are conditional computational relationships, not newly measured battery performance.

evidence.tested: More than 120,000 candidate structures screened before 1,025 first-principles calculations; five single-metal and ten equimolar mixed-metal chemistries. Selected comparisons use previously published measurements.
evidence.unknown: Restricted ordering library, selected stackings and equimolar mixtures; zero-temperature energetics omit entropy and kinetic effects. Learned preselection may miss alternatives. Moment-derived oxidation states have covalency ambiguity and some experimental disagreements. No cycling-performance or universal composition prediction is established.
evidence.ai_role: MACE relaxes and ranks stacking alternatives, determining which candidates proceed to first-principles analysis; downstream redox interpretation uses those selected structures.

source_review.scope: Actual v1 primary computational selection Methods, comparative redox Results and discussion limitations; v1 October22 already contains represented result, later v2 October26 distinguished.
